ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (2024 Revision, effective January 1, 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information issued by the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation under Order No. 3 [2024], effective November 1, 2024; Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2020); Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Order No. 746); PBOC Order [2021] No. 1, Administrative Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Supervision of Financial Institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the PRC WFOE (Business License / foreign-invested enterprise legal person registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or the competent local Municipal Market Regulation Administration where the WFOE is registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use in an Apostille Convention state: notarize the Chinese business license by a notary public in mainland China, then obtain a PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille or an apostille issued by an authorized provincial foreign affairs office. For use in Taiwan or another non-Apostille state: use the parallel pathway of notarization plus SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification or consular legalization at the competent consular office; do not chain a Hague apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / enterprise credit information disclosure report for the PRC WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the receiving jurisdiction is party to the Hague Apostille Convention, the SAMR-certified printout must be notarized and then apostilled by the competent PRC foreign affairs authority. If the receiving jurisdiction is Taiwan or another non-member state, the document must be notarized and then verified through ARATS/SEF or legalized by the destination consulate; the Hague Apostille path and consular legalization path are alternatives and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney of the Taiwan investor authorizing the WFOE formation and the local filing agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan-resident investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan-issued corporate documents cannot receive a PRC-recognized Hague apostille because Taiwan is not a party to the Apostille Convention. The correct parallel path is: notarize the board resolution before a Taiwan notary, then have the notarial certificate verified by the Straits Exchange Foundation and cross-confirmed by ARATS/consular authorities in mainland China; for any other non-Hague state, use Taiwan Economic and Cultural Office consular legalization rather than an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (amended and restated for the PRC WFOE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All shareholders of the PRC WFOE and approved/recorded by SAMR as part of the formation dossier
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized Chinese articles of association may, where a foreign government requires proof of registration, be notarized and then apostilled by the PRC MFA for use in Apostille Convention member states. For use in Taiwan, the articles must be verified through the ARATS/SEF cross-strait channel or consular legalization, depending on the destination authority; the two authentication mechanisms are mutually exclusive and parallel.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from the WFOE's proposed or existing commercial bank confirming account history, credit conduct, and AML compliance standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed commercial bank in mainland China or the Taiwan investor's relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A bank letter is a private banking instrument; it must be issued within 90 days and, if required by the receiving regulator, signed by an authorized bank officer before a notary. Once notarized, a PRC-issued letter can be apostilled for an Apostille Convention destination or consular-legalized for a non-member destination; a Taiwan-issued letter follows TECO consular legalization / SEF-ARATS verification and not a Hague apostille. Never apply both methods to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Legalized/verified investor identification and authorization set (passport/corporate register excerpt of the ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and legal representatives)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs commercial registration office and/or notarized individual identity records issued by Taiwanese notaries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Because Taiwan is not an Apostille Contracting Party, UBO identity documentation destined for use in mainland China should be notarized in Taiwan and thereafter verified through the SEF/ARATS mechanism or, if a non-Apostille third country is involved, through consular legalization at the competent TECO/embassy; PRC-issued UBO identity documents for use abroad would instead receive a PRC apostille only when the receiving state is an Apostille Convention state.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The filing bank, SAMR-supervised formation agent, and external counsel must screen every shareholder, director, legal representative, authorized signatory, and beneficial owner against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sectoral sanctions lists including Ukraine/Russia and PRC-military-industrial complex designations, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, PRC Ministry of Public Security and SAMR regulatory blacklists, the Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act watchlist, and the central bank's PEP database. Any positive or fuzzy match triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, corporate-ownership diagramming, adverse media review, and risk-based escalation to the AML compliance officer; no account may be opened or formation certificate issued until the screening false-positive review is completed and documented.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Pre-registration and Self-Service Declaration Portal (integrated with the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and provincial market regulation administration government-service portals)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name of a PRC WFOE must be in simplified Chinese characters; an English name may be registered for operational use but does not replace the Chinese legal name. The name must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive name + industry/operation descriptive words + company type designation. Foreign investor transliterations must follow standard Mandarin phonetic conventions, avoid negative homophones, and be clearly distinguishable from existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a written name rejection, the applicant may submit an administrative reconsideration request to the SAMR registration authority or its next higher market regulation administration within 15 days of notice, under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, attaching the rejection notice, the intended name, and a legal memorandum on availability. If reconsideration fails, an administrative lawsuit

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (Republic of China), as amended, Articles 1, 10, 18, 98, 99, 100, 101, 108, 128, 129, 156, 208, 387, and 437; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 4, 7, and 8; Banking Act of Taiwan, Article 3, as applied to capital remittance and escrow accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (Company Registration Section and Foreign Investment Coordination Unit of the Investment Commission, MOEA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Company, together with the Articles of Incorporation, filed through the MOEA Company Registration Information System.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Taiwan Company Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a software or cloud-services limited company. However, because this is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, the foreign investment approval granted by the Investment Commission must be used to remit the subscribed capital into Taiwan before the registration filing. The remitted capital is held in a temporary foreign exchange capital reserve bank account and cannot be disbursed for ordinary operating expenses until the CPA issues the Capital Verification Report and the company registration certificate is granted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the incorporation and registration process of the Company, as identified in the Articles of Incorporation, be and the same is hereby ratified, confirmed, and caused to proceed with full force and effect.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the initial shareholders and subscribers hereto acknowledge the subscription of the issued share capital of the Company, as set forth in the subscribed capital schedule, and authorize the directors to receive the paid-in amounts and to issue share certificates in accordance with the Taiwan Company Act, and to make such filings with the Department of Commercial Affairs of the Ministry of Economic Affairs as may be required.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company located at [insert full Taiwan address] be and the same is hereby adopted as the statutory registered office of the Company, and the Company authorizes the use of such office for all official communications, notices, service of process, and statutory record-keeping.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name A], [Name B], [Name C], and [Name D] shall be and hereby are appointed as the first Directors, with [Name A] serving as Chairperson, and [Name D] serving as Company Secretary and Local Manager for the purposes of Taiwan company law compliance, including the maintenance of the shareholder register, minutes book, and corporate seal.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairperson, together with any one Director, or any two Directors jointly, are authorized to open, operate, and close bank accounts housed in the Company's name with one or more financial institutions approved under the Banking Act of Taiwan, and to sign all cheques, wire transfer instructions, and banking mandates.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company file its tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau, obtain a uniform invoice statement where applicable, and appoint an internal controller for withholding tax obligations.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company shall comply with all applicable labor, occupational health, building, and fire safety laws for its registered office and software development premises, and that no manufacturing, chemical production, or warehousing activities shall be undertaken absent separate environmental and civil defense licensing.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairperson is authorized to execute any and all documents, indemnities, contracts, and lease agreements in connection with the incorporation proceeding and to reimburse incorporation expenses upon proper evidence.

RESOLVED, that these resolutions shall remain in full force and effect until amended or revoked by a subsequent resolution of the shareholders or directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name pre-clearance and lawful business scope alignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (online Company Name Pre-screening and Business Registration E-Service portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-incorporation name and business scope review. Submit a name pre-approval application to the Department of Commercial Affairs of the Ministry of Economic Affairs through the industry and commerce registration service. The proposed name must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered trademark or company. Prepare a clear English and/or Chinese name, identify the primary business as computer programming activities, data processing, hosting, and related activities under ISIC 6201, and select a lawful registered entity type described as a Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Company. Approval of the name should be obtained before submitting substantive incorporation documents. Any material change to the business scope after registration will require a subsequent amendment filing.
required_dossiers: Name pre-approval application form
Shareholder passport or foreign company certificate of incorporation, notarized where requested
Statement of proposed business scope and permitted items
Written authorization of the incorporation agent, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or public-interest grounds, the applicant may file a formal objection with the Department of Commercial Affairs within ten working days, or alternatively submit a revised name and reapply at the same portal. Any examiner query must be answered in writing within the period stated in the notice; failure to do so is curable by a fresh application without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (Foreign Investment Review Desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs for permission to invest in Taiwan as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise. Because the WFOE is wholly foreign-owned and under foreign shareholders, the foreign investment application is mandatory. The application must include the shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner certificate of incorporation, audited financial statements or bank reference, capital remittance plan, and a declaration confirming that the business does not relate to any restricted or prohibited sector under Taiwanese law. The Investment Commission will issue an investment approval letter setting out the permissible shareholding percentage, approved foreign capital amount, and conditions. This approval is a condition precedent to capital remittance and final company registration.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment application form for foreign investors
Notarized foreign company registration or shareholder identification documents
Business plan and feasibility statement
Financial statements or bank reference evidencing source of funds
Final-form Articles of Incorporation
Declaration confirming no engagement in restricted or prohibited industries
Power of attorney appointing the local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a deficiency or suspension notice, the applicant has thirty days from the date of notice to supply the requested documents. If the application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs Petition Committee within thirty days after service of the rejection decision, or re-submit after remedying the stated grounds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital remittance, bank account opening, and CPA capital verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized foreign exchange bank in Taiwan, Central Bank of China reporting channel, and a licensed Taiwan Certified Public Accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary foreign currency capital reserve account at a licensed bank in Taiwan, remit the foreign-investment approved capital, and convert the funds into New Taiwan Dollars. Upon conversion, the bank issues a remittance certificate and a foreign exchange settlement confirmation. A Taiwan CPA then conducts the capital verification and issues the Capital Verification Report, which is required by the Department of Commercial Affairs for company registration. The verification report must confirm that the capital was paid into the company bank account in cash or through equivalent approved monetary instruments and must match the foreign investment approval. This step must be completed within the validity period of the investment approval letter.
required_dossiers: Investment approval letter from the Investment Commission
Foreign exchange conversion application as prescribed by the bank
Bank remittance slips or SWIFT MT103 equivalent
Instructions to the CPA for capital verification
Bank balance confirmation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or CPA queries the remittance due to incomplete documentation, the applicant must supply the original foreign exchange settlement certificate or correspond through the authorized bank with the Central Bank of China. Any excess capital held in the temporary account must be refunded or segregated until the approved amount is verified; administrative correction may be made by a supplemental CPA confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal company registration filing with the Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (Company Registration Information System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the formal company registration application through the company registration information system. The application package must include the name pre-approval certificate, the foreign investment approval letter, the CPA capital verification report, the articles of incorporation, the registered office designation, the list of directors and the chairperson, and the corporate seal card if applicable. The registrar will examine the legality of the corporate name, scope, capital, and governance structure. Upon approval, the MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate, which evidences legal personality from the registration date. Signed minutes of the directors resolution, consent of the directors, and passport or national identity card scans must be attached in searchable PDF format.
required_dossiers: Company registration application form
Articles of Incorporation stamped or signed by all subscribers
Name pre-approval certificate
Foreign investment approval letter
CPA capital verification report
List of directors and chairperson with signed consent to act
Registered office address consent or building usage consent
Board resolution authorizing the registration filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration examiner issues a supplementary notice, the applicant has fifteen days to cure omissions. If the application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within thirty days after service of the rejection, or directly amend and resubmit the application after satisfying the examiner objection and paying any required resubmission fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, labor registration, and post-incorporation compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, National Health Insurance Administration, Ministry of Labor, and local municipal government building/fire administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete tax registration and post-incorporation authorizations. Within fifteen days after the company is registered, apply to the National Taxation Bureau for the Tax Identification Number, uniform invoice stock, and an invoice booklet if the company will sell services in Taiwan. Register with the National Health Insurance Administration and the Ministry of Labor for labor insurance and pension contribution payments for employees. Apply for building occupancy inspection certificates and fire safety equipment maintenance reports where required by the local municipal government. For the approved cloud software services, no physical operating license is required, but the company should adopt and publish a personal data protection policy and register any high-volume personal data file with the competent authority if applicable.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate
Foreign investment approval letter
Tax identification number application form
Passport or national identity card of the responsible person
Lease agreement or registered office address proof
Business scope description and service catalog
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed or queried, the company may file a late registration application with the National Taxation Bureau and pay the statutory penalty, then submit a written explanation accompanied by supporting evidence to request penalty reduction. Where operational delays prevent timely labor or health registration, the company should promptly seek a grace period confirmation from the respective authorities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The registered business activity is software development and cloud-based developer infrastructure under ISIC 6201, which does not fall within the jurisdiction of the industrial licensing authorities for manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No industrial manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operating license is required for the approved DevOps/cloud tools business scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan, and the local municipal environmental protection department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable and exempt. The project is a software and cloud infrastructure service with no physical manufacturing, no construction of an industrial plant, no wastewater discharge, and no land development exceeding the threshold requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment under Article 4 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The operation will produce no process wastewater, no volatile organic compound fugitive emissions, no stationary combustion source, and no hazardous industrial waste. General office waste must be handled under the Waste Disposal Act, and indoor air quality in the leased office must meet the applicable minimum standards under the Indoor Air Quality Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for manufacturing clearance; however, the Company must obtain an office building fire safety certification from the local fire department under Article 6 and Article 9 of the Fire Services Act, maintain fire prevention equipment, file an occupational safety and health self-assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, and comply with the Building Act requirements for office occupancy, including maximum floor load and means-of-escape inspection certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); the official online electronic filing portal is the China Electronic Tax Administration e-Tax platform (Electronic Tax Bureau), accessible through the STA and provincial tax service bureaus. For this CN_WFOE_LTD, Taiwan (TW) is the cross-strait investor/offshore jurisdiction; unless a Taiwan branch or permanent establishment is separately registered, Taiwan is not the registration jurisdiction for this China-domiciled WFOE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the business license containing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) for all People's Republic of China tax filings, including Corporate Income Tax (CIT), Value-Added Tax (VAT), and withholding tax. Step 2: Within 30 calendar days from the date of business license issuance, complete the tax registration information confirmation in the provincial Electronic Tax Bureau platform; the system automatically synchronizes the SAMR registration to the tax authority and activates the tax registration file. Step 3: Register the entity's VAT taxpayer status with the competent tax service bureau; the default is small-scale taxpayer if annual taxable sales do not exceed RMB 5,000,000, but the WFOE may apply for general VAT taxpayer status to claim input VAT credits and support export zero-rating. Step 4: If the ultimate parent or Taiwan investor will receive China-source dividends, royalties, interest, or service fees, the WFOE as payer must complete a non-resident enterprise filing in the electronic tax bureau and, where required, obtain/record the non-resident taxpayer identification number for withholding CIT and VAT on cross-border payments. Step 5: For export zero-rating of cloud/software services, complete the cross-border taxable services zero-rating/exemption record-filing with the competent tax authority by uploading the service contract, non-resident recipient evidence, and anticipated payment terms. Step 6: Maintain a dedicated tax account and compliance folder for invoice issuance, general ledger, export documentation, and foreign-exchange receipts (FIRC/SAFE records).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the China WFOE is a resident enterprise of the People's Republic of China and is taxed on worldwide income at the entity level under the Corporate Income Tax Law; it is not an eligible pass-through entity. VAT is collected separately on taxable supplies; the WFOE is not a tax-exempt zone entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for US-style check-the-box; China has no domestic check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election under normal Chinese tax law. Available statutory elections are: (a) election to become a general VAT taxpayer when below the RMB 5,000,000 threshold; (b) election to remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer using simplified levy rates when eligible; (c) election to apply the reduced small-and-low-profit CIT regime if the statutory thresholds for annual taxable income, asset value, and headcount are met; (d) record-filing election for cross-border taxable services zero-rating/exemption. No hybrid mismatch election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Law of the People's Republic of China and its implementing regulations, including the STA cross-border taxable services zero-rating/exemption rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover threshold for tax registration: every WFOE must register with the STA within 30 days of SAMR incorporation. The mandatory economic threshold triggering general VAT taxpayer registration is annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 (five million yuan); below that threshold the entity may remain a small-scale taxpayer. Domestic cloud/software services are generally subject to 6% VAT, while domestic goods sales are generally subject to 13% VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory real-time electronic invoice clearance regime. The WFOE

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a controlled but progressively managed convertibility regime. Current account transactions, including software subscription exports, service fees, and dividend remittances, are broadly convertible and do not require SAFE pre-approval after the underlying real-business authenticity is verified by a designated FX bank. Profit repatriation by a WFOE to overseas shareholders is permitted once annual statutory audit, tax clearance, and a board dividend resolution are completed; a withholding tax of 10% applies unless a double tax agreement lowers the rate. There is no mandatory surrender or fixed conversion ratio for export proceeds, but all trade-related FX receipts must be repatriated into a domestic FX settlement account within the statutory period (normally 90 days from export or service performance) and can be converted into RMB under the bank booking model. Capital account convertibility remains constrained: inbound FDI requires SAFE foreign exchange registration and a dedicated capital account; funds credited to the capital account can be converted to RMB only for transactions within the WFOE's business scope and are prohibited from being used for equity investment or securities speculation unless specifically approved. Outbound capital flows for acquisitions or lending are subject to SAFE approval and project filing. Therefore the WFOE should treat its domestic RMB books as operationally current-account convertible, but must maintain strict documentation of the OFDI/FDI reporting trail for any capital account movement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE regulations, all foreign export receipts must be repatriated to a designated bank account in the People's Republic of China. There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio; the WFOE may keep the earnings in foreign currency or convert to RMB. For goods exports, statutory collection is generally 90 days from the customs declaration date, unless a longer credit term is reported to SAFE. For service exports (software/cloud), receipts must be collected in accordance with the underlying contract and presented to the bank with invoice and service evidence. Receipts not collected within 90 days (or the reported expected date) require a revised trade credit report and supporting documents.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI capital account) for foreign-invested enterprise

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (RMB current account)
Foreign Currency Settlement Account for trade receipts and disbursements
Multi-currency treasury account with onshore FX hedging derivatives

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low / Not Viable as onshore treasury settlement bank. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Mercury, Stripe Billing, Wise, Airwallex and Revolut do not hold a banking license from PBOC/SAFE and cannot open domestic RMB/FX settlement accounts for a mainland WFOE. They cannot receive registered capital or act as the clearing bank for export proceeds and service-trade FX payments because all such transactions must be settled through a licensed Chinese bank within SAFE's reporting system. Such EMIs may be used only as a product/billing interface (e.g., Stripe for collecting customer card payments outside mainland) provided funds are ultimately routed through a licensed cross-border payment provider or the WFOE's licensed Chinese bank. Relying on Mercury ACH as a treasury rail would violate foreign exchange administration and PBOC AML rules, and may result in fines and account suspension.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance by the legal representative is mandatory to open the basic RMB current account; a remote consular proxy is not legally sufficient. For a Taiwan-appointed legal representative, they would need to attend in person at the mainland bank branch (or via a mainland-appointed authorized representative with original notarized power of attorney and Chinese translation). The bank will conduct a face-to-face interview and may carry out site inspection. If the legal representative is outside China, the WFOE should arrange a visa and bank appointment; some banks permit video-call identity verification only as an additional step, not as a substitute.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) caused by a cross-border ownership chain from Taiwan through one or more intermediate holding vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificates of incorporation, shareholder registers and director registers for every intermediate entity; notarized UBO declaration listing all natural persons holding above 10%; identity documents and utility bills; independent legal opinion confirming the chain; and a complete group structure chart matching the SAFE onshore FDI foreign exchange registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming registered capital remittances from bank accounts not matching the registered foreign investor name, or showing round-tripping through financial-institution concentration accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original SWIFT MT103 advice showing the remitter name exactly equal to the SAFE-registered shareholder; 12-month bank statements of the remitter; board resolution authorizing capital contribution; source-of-wealth statement (dividends distribution, sales proceeds, disposal of shares, loan agreement); remittance contract; tax-paid evidence on funds; and a written confirmation that no shell/offshore conduit is in an FATF grey-list jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legal representative and actual controller mismatch plus lack of physical substance in mainland (virtual office, no staff).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Appointment resolution of the statutory legal representative; PRC identity card or passport with residence permit; copy of the registered office lease with recent rent and utility invoices; social security payroll list of employees; company seal issuance record; and, in the case of a nominee, a power of attorney and personal guarantee from the actual controller.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected contradiction between the declared DevOps/cloud business scope and the FX settlement pattern (e.g., high-value receipts without service contracts or with mismatched counterparties).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master SaaS/cloud agreements with clients, periodic invoices with service descriptions, payment evidence from client banks, transaction-level cloud infrastructure consumption reports, annual audit report, and PRC VAT and Corporate Income Tax filings proving the transaction lifecycle; if embedded goods are present, provide customs declarations and logistics documents.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity injection, the overseas parent remits via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's FDI capital account at the designated Chinese bank. The remittance narrative must state equity investment/registered capital under the SAFE FDI registration, and the bank will map this to the appropriate Balance of Payments and SAFE transaction code for foreign direct investment. The receiving bank verifies the remitter against the SAFE registration, checks the negative list, then credits the capital account. Funds may be settled into RMB for within-scope use via the Foreign Exchange Capital Settlement System. Although the current PRC Company Law does not mandate a minimum registered capital for an ordinary WFOE, declared capital must be remitted within the business term and supported by a bank receipt; a Chinese CPA capital verification report should be prepared if required by the bank or lenders, and any difference between completed and registered capital must be recorded by updating the SAFE FDI registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For services (cloud infrastructure, software subscriptions, APIs), the WFOE submits the underlying contract, commercial invoice, and tax clearance certificate for service-trade cross-border payments above USD 50,000; the designated bank debits the FX settlement account and sends SWIFT MT103. For physical goods or high-value license purchases, the company may use a Commercial Letter of Credit or Documentary Collections if the supplier requests banker's undertaking; otherwise MT103 remains the primary rail. annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly withholding tax remittance statement and tax equalization filing for salaries, directors' fees, dividends, royalties, and other taxable payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Local Branch), Ministry of Finance, Republic of China
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 10th day of the month immediately following the month in which the withholding obligation arises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest of 1% per month on the unpaid amount plus an educational and cultural surcharge of 2%; under-withholding penalty of 20% of the un-withheld tax; administrative enforcement, bank levy, and asset seizure may commence 30 days after formal demand.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bi-monthly value-added business tax (Business Tax Act) return and Uniform Invoice voucher submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Local Branch), Ministry of Finance, Republic of China
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th day of the month following each two-month filing period: 15 Mar, 15 May, 15 Jul, 15 Sep, 15 Nov, and 15 Jan for the preceding two-month period; if the 15th falls on a national holiday, the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 1% of the tax due for every 2-day delay, capped at 10%; late payment interest at 1% per month; chronic failure may lead to cancellation of Uniform Invoice registration and administrative strike-off of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return and financial-statement annex (Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Act Articles 71-76)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Republic of China
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal-year 2025 calendar-year return must be filed between 1 May 2026 and 31 May 2026; extension applications accepted before the statutory filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 3% of unpaid tax for each additional 2-month interval, maximum 9%; late payment interest at 1% per month; after 30 days the tax authority may attach bank accounts, freeze receivables, and commence administrative compulsory execution; fraudulent or false filing is subject to criminal penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting, approval of final accounts, and submission of meeting minutes and the business report (Company Act Articles 20, 228, 230)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the WFOE; minutes and financial statements subsequently filed with Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must be held no later than 30 June following the fiscal year end for a calendar-year company; minutes and final accounts must be filed within 15 days after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting or obtain statutory approval exposes the responsible person to an administrative fine of NTD 10,000 - 50,000 per violation; repeated refusal or failure may trigger an MOEA order for dissolution or strike-off of the company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual company information declaration of major shareholders, directors, supervisors, managers, and significant controllers (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Company Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding calendar year; any transfer of shares causing a change in a 10%-or-more shareholder, or any change of director, supervisor, manager, or major controller, must be filed within 15 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing false or incomplete information subjects the representative to fines of NTD 10,000 - 50,000 per instance; falsification may constitute professional misconduct and, in serious cases, lead to revocation of company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified independent CPA audit and financial statement certification where statutory thresholds are met (Company Act Article 20; Securities and Exchange Act if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent CPA firm licensed in Taiwan; audited statements filed with the National Taxation Bureau with the annual income tax return and submitted to MOEA with the annual shareholders' meeting minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the annual shareholders' meeting, normally by 30 June for calendar-year entities; if required for tax filing, audited statements must accompany the income tax return by 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a compulsory CPA audit may cause rejection of annual registration, disallowance of net operating loss carryforwards, and fines for unqualified financial statements of up to NTD 600,000; knowingly certifying false books attracts CPA license suspension and criminal liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 20 and the Regulations on Commercial Accounting and Financial Statements, an independent CPA audit is mandatory for: (1) public companies and securities issuers under the Securities and Exchange Act; (2) private non-public companies whose paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million; (3) private companies whose outstanding bank loans exceed NT$30 million at fiscal year end; (4) companies whose annual operating revenue exceeds NT$100 million (approximately USD 3.3 million); (5) companies required by the Ministry of Economic Affairs or the tax authority to have audited statements due to public-interest or industry-risk reasons; (6) companies whose foreign parent or group auditor requires audited standalone financial statements for consolidated TIFRS/IFRS reporting; and (7) companies applying for certain bank credit facilities or government contracts that condition approval on audited financials. An ISIC 6201 cloud-tools WFOE with a global parent and consolidated IFRS filing will ordinarily trigger audit because of parent-imposed group audit requirements even if the local NT$30 million capital threshold is not exceeded.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Taiwan International Financial Reporting Standards (TIFRS), which are the IFRS Standards as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission, for companies required to publish audited financial statements; entities below the statutory audit thresholds may elect to follow the Taiwan SME Accounting Standards (SME GAAP), but for a foreign-owned entity in the cloud infrastructure sector, group policies and cross-border financing covenants typically mandate TIFRS. The tax return is reconciled separately using the Income Tax Act basis schedules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the WFOE must annually declare to the Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commerce by 31 March the names, national IDs, shareholdings, and positions of all directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding more than 10% of the issued shares. Any share transfer that causes a 10%-or-greater shareholder to change, or any appointment/resignation of directors, supervisors, or managers, must be reported within 15 days of the event. For beneficial ownership, the Money Laundering Control Act and the Company Act require the company to identify and keep on file the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners of shares held through nominees, trusts, or offshore structures; material changes in beneficial ownership must be reflected in the next Article 22-1 annual declaration. Taiwan does not require a separate annual UBO certificate, but the registered office must maintain KYC and UBO identification records for audit by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, tax authorities, and the Financial Supervisory Commission for five to seven years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% profit-seeking enterprise income tax, plus a separate 5% retained-earnings surcharge on undistributed earnings if profits are not distributed; the effective aggregate cost structure for a Taiwan WFOE is therefore 20% corporate tax plus either the 5% retained-earnings surcharge or the 21% non-resident dividend withholding tax at distribution.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible incentives for a DevOps/cloud infrastructure WFOE include: (i) the R&D investment tax credit under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, generally up to 20% of qualifying R&D expenditures, capped at 30% of the current-year profit-seeking enterprise income tax payable and usable over the next 10 years; (ii) a 5-year profit-seeking enterprise income tax holiday for qualifying new investments in designated innovative industries where statutory conditions and local substance thresholds are met; (iii) Taiwan Free Trade Zone incentives, which primarily cover import duty exemption, deferred customs processing, and certain investment credits; (iv) accelerated depreciation for qualifying software, server hardware, and network infrastructure assets; and (v) no formal patent-box regime, but IP-derived income from own software exploitation may benefit indirectly from R&D credits, Section 20 research deductions, and careful transfer pricing of the economic ownership of cloud APIs and monitoring database software.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return (the unified annual corporate income tax return for resident enterprises and non-resident branches), filed electronically through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance tax e-filing portal at https://www.tax.nat.gov.tw, with authenticated electronic certificate or tax agent authorization.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return, together with quarterly estimated profit-seeking enterprise income tax prepayments due in June, September, December, and April; monthly withholding tax statements for payments made to non-residents are due by the 10th day following the month of payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the annual return must be filed from 1 May to 31 May of the following year, with the electronic filing deadline at 23:59 on 31 May; for an approved non-calendar fiscal year, the return is due within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year-end; quarterly estimated prepayments are due respectively by 30 June, 30 September, 31 December, and 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Filing Status, Taxpayer Identity, and Fiscal Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, uniform profit-seeking enterprise certificate number, head-office address, tax file number, line of business, and the annual accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan-incorporated WFOE is a resident profit-seeking enterprise and must report worldwide income. If the WFOE operates as a branch or permanent establishment of a foreign corporation instead of a local subsidiary, the non-resident branch schedule must be used to report Taiwan-source SaaS subscription income, database fees, API monitoring charges, and after-allowance expenses. Any foreign parent providing services to the Taiwan entity through remote servers or overseas engineers should be assessed for a Taiwan permanent establishment risk, especially if contracts are concluded through a fixed place of business in Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Gross Revenue and Business Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from software subscription licenses, database hosting, API monitoring, infrastructure-as-a-service, maintenance fees, technical support services, and any related consulting services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize cloud subscription revenue over the contract term; do not defer it in a way that shifts taxable income to a China parent or offshore affiliate. State content and sales-use tax separately where applicable. Fees from non-resident related parties must be priced at arm's length and evidenced by signed intercompany agreements, delivery tickets, usage logs, and invoices; otherwise the National Tax Administration may add the revenue back to Taiwan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Cost of Goods Sold and Direct Cost Allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs such as cloud server hosting, co-location costs, bandwidth, electricity, hardware depreciation, third-party software licenses, and direct labor costs of DevOps engineers attributable to the service delivery function.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE purchases cloud infrastructure, servers, or API technology from a related offshore parent, the costs must meet the arm's length standard and remain within Taiwan transfer pricing documentation thresholds. If no contemporaneous TP report is prepared when mandatory, the tax authority may disallow a portion of these costs under the general anti-avoidance rule and may reclassify them as royalties subject to 20% withholding, creating an additional tax, interest, and penalty exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Operating Expenses: Sales, Marketing, General Administration, and R&D
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local salaries, rent, legal and accounting fees, marketing expenses, insurance, office depreciation, employee training, and research and development expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must demonstrate economic substance through employment contracts, payroll tax filings, labor pension contributions, rent payments, board minutes, and management decisions actually taking place in Taiwan. Allocations of group head-office or China-parent overhead are deductible only if supported by service agreements, actual benefits received, itemized cost invoices, and no double-charge to other group entities. Intangible-related development costs should be documented via contemporaneous cost-sharing or licensing agreements to prevent an offshore recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign exchange gains and losses, gains and losses on disposal of fixed assets, royalty income, dividend income, and other non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For interest and royalty income received by the Taiwan WFOE, the source rule is generally the residency of the payer or the place where the IP is used; non-resident withholding taxes may apply to payments made to the WFOE by Taiwan residents. Accrued interest on intercompany borrowing must be supported by written loan agreements, market rates, and proper withholding if paid to a foreign lender; excessive related-party debt may trigger thin-capitalization disallowance under Income Tax Act Article 43-2.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss available under Income Tax Act Article 39, deducted from the current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses incurred after 2009 may be carried forward for 10 years if the taxpayer maintains sufficient accounting records and has filed timely, valid returns. The loss carryforward is deducted only against taxable income of the resident Taiwan entity; it does not alter or reduce dividend withholding tax on profits distributed to non-resident shareholders. In a WFOE group restructuring, preserve the continuity of the taxable entity and proper business purpose to avoid the loss deduction being challenged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Taxable Income Calculation and Regular Corporate Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all deductions, exemptions, and loss carryforwards; application of the 20% headline rate; calculation of the basic tax amount before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same taxable income is subject to the alternative minimum tax at 12% on the excess over the NT$6,000,000 exemption, if the alternative minimum tax exceeds the regular tax. A WFOE must reconcile financial statement book income with tax return income and separately report permanent differences such as non-deductible penalties and unrecognized foreign exchange movements. Any adjustment made by the tax authority to the gross margin will flow through this line and materially affect quarterly estimated prepayments and final tax payable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Investment Tax Credits, R&D Credits, and Foreign Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for qualifying R&D expenditures, employee training, energy-saving investments, and foreign income taxes paid on income also reported in Taiwan.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document every R&D credit with project descriptions, staff time records, and qualified expense ledgers. Foreign tax credits are available on a unilateral basis only for foreign-source income actually reported in Taiwan; Chinese or other offshore taxes on the same income must be evidenced by a foreign tax assessment or withholding certificate. Credits cannot be applied against the 21% withholding tax owed on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Retained Earnings Surtax / Undistributed Surplus Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of current-year earnings, reserves, dividends distributed, and undistributed retained earnings; computation of the 5% retained-earnings surcharge on undistributed amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders often prefer a distribution in the following calendar year to trigger the 21% dividend withholding tax rather than allowing the Taiwan entity to bear the 5% retained-earnings surcharge. The dividend declaration must be approved by the board and shareholders before the year-end planning date. If the WFOE attempts to characterize a dividend as a service fee or repayment of a fake loan to avoid distribution WHT, the tax authority will recharacterize the payment and impose the full 21% WHT, late-interest, and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Withholding Tax Credits, Quarterly Prepayments, and Net Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for quarterly estimated income tax prepayments and any Taiwan-source withholding tax credits actually attributed to the same year's income; final net tax payable or overpayment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All prior-year estimated payments must be supported by bank payment records and e-filing vouchers. The WFOE must not claim a credit for withholding tax on outbound dividends or royalties that were withheld from non-residents; those amounts are liabilities of the payee, not credits of the Taiwan entity. If the final tax exceeds the quarterly prepayments by more than 20%, the shortfall may be subject to delayed-interest charges as prescribed by the Tax Collection Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Related-Party Disclosure and Transfer Pricing Report
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete the related-party transaction schedule, including intercompany purchases, sales, service fees, royalty payments, interest payments, management charges, and the selected transfer pricing methodology.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A contemporaneous transfer pricing report is required when the Taiwan WFOE's annual related-party transactions exceed NT$200,000,000 or where cross-border controlled transactions are otherwise significant; master file and local file requirements accompany group consolidated revenue thresholds for Country-by-Country reporting, generally at NT$54,000,000,000 for the ultimate parent group. In the absence of a qualifying transfer pricing study, the tax authority may use any reasonable OECD method to impute taxable income, including a routine return on costs and assets, thereby stripping from the WFOE any profit attributable to group intangibles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Non-Resident Payments and Withholding Reconciliation Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed schedule of dividends, interest, royalties, rentals, and compensation paid to non-resident persons, along with withholding tax rates applied, tax withheld, and the date of tax payment to the National Tax Administration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If payments to a China resident shareholder or a China parent are intended to benefit from relief under the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation, the beneficial owner must hold a tax residence certificate, demonstrate economic substance and beneficial ownership, and obtain approval for the reduced rate before remittance. If no reduced rate is approved, dividends must be withheld at 21%, and interest and royalties at 20%, with the withheld tax paid to the treasury by the 10th day of the following month. A WFOE that fails to reconcile the statutory WHT on its Box 12 schedule will trigger the penalty provisions of Income Tax Act Article 114 and immediate use of debt-collection and travel-ban measures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual income tax return triggers Income Tax Act Article 108: a penalty equal to 10% of the unpaid tax (with a minimum penalty of NT$1,500) if tax is due, or a NT$600 to NT$900 penalty if no tax is due, plus monthly interest on the delinquency; late filing with intent to evade triggers Article 110, which authorizes an additional penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax. Forgery of invoices, use of fictitious vendors, or intentional omission of aggregated cloud subscription revenue are treated as criminal tax evasion under Tax Collection Act Article 41, punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years, criminal detention, and/or a fine as adjusted by judicial interpretation. Willful failure to withhold and pay non-resident withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties results in a penalty of not less than 10% and not more than 20% of the amount underwithheld, in addition to the tax itself, and can expose the responsible director to a blacklisting/travel-ban order under Tax Collection Act Article 24 when unpaid tax arrears exceed NT$300,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% withholding tax on dividends paid or distributed to non-resident shareholders (including non-resident individuals and non-resident profit-seeking enterprises) under Income Tax Act Article 88 and Article 26; dividends paid to a resident corporate shareholder are generally not subject to 21% withholding, while resident individuals receiving dividends are integrated into the personal income tax system with the imputation credit mechanism abolished and no separate dividend withholding at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke bilateral DTA or Cross-Strait agreement relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate for the relevant calendar year from the competent tax authority of the residence jurisdiction, or for a China resident investor, a China tax resident certificate issued by the State Taxation Administration; (ii) submit a beneficial ownership declaration supported by board resolutions, audited financial statements, employee/payroll records, office leases, and operating evidence proving the shareholder is not a conduit, pass-through, or back-to-back nominee; (iii) provide an organizational chart showing the direct and indirect ownership chain; (iv) file the application for reduced withholding rate with the National Tax Administration before distribution, or, where the full 21% dividend tax is withheld, submit a refund application with the same documentation for post-remittance relief; and (v) if the China resident beneficial owner directly holds at least 25% of the shares of the Taiwan WFOE for at least 365 days, the dividend withholding rate may be reduced to 5%; in all other beneficial ownership cases the reduced rate is 10%. Without prior administrative approval or a successful refund application, the Taiwan payer must withhold and remit the full 21% statutory rate. Relief is strictly denied where the recipient lacks economic substance in its residence jurisdiction, because the Taiwan tax administration will apply the Limitation on Benefits and general anti-abuse doctrines embedded in the cross-strait arrangement and Tax Collection Act practice.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding rates on outbound interest and royalties paid by a Taiwan WFOE to a non-resident are 20% for interest and 20% for royalties under Income Tax Act Article 88. Under an approved bilateral double taxation agreement, or under the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation where administratively implemented for China-Taiwan transactions, interest and royalties paid to the China beneficial owner may be reduced to 7% (with rates depending on the type of IP and payment stream) provided the recipient files a tax residence certificate, proves beneficial ownership, meets the Limitation on Benefits clause, and obtains the reduced-rate approval before remittance. If the Taiwan WFOE is thinly capitalized, interest deductions on loans from related parties are disallowed under Income Tax Act Article 43-2 where the debt-to-equity ratio exceeds 3:1, and the disallowed interest may be recharacterized as a dividend subject to 21% withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$200,000,000 of aggregate annual related-party transactions is the statutory threshold triggering mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and a transfer pricing report in New Taiwan Dollars; enterprises with lower transaction amounts should still prepare documentary evidence for Code 43-1 audits. Master File and Local File schedules become compulsory when the Taiwan WFOE's related-party transactions exceed the de minimis threshold or when the ultimate parent group reports
